cited_evidence: Top-level input includes record_id n06-r06 with demand_score 5, need "compare selected and complete runtime evidence", source_id s06, source_weight 3.
Behavioural criteria require selecting all qualifying or fallback demand records and retaining only allowed record identities without silently omitting stipulated records.
select_demand source selects corpus rows where demand_score >= 3 or record_id is in fallback_ids, so n06-r06 qualifies by score.
normalize source defines allowed_record_ids as ['n06-r01','n06-r02','n06-r03','n06-r04','n06-r05','n06-r09','n06-r07','n06-r08'], omitting n06-r06.
job_1 output needs and evidence_sources contain n06-r01 through n06-r05, n06-r07, and n06-r08, but not n06-r06.
job_2 metadata reports consumed_handoffs ['needs','evidence_sources'], and its output consistently reflects the seven-record upstream input.
initial_receipt.explanation: The two-job execution contains a fault because the upstream job silently omitted qualifying demand record n06-r06. The top-level corpus includes n06-r06 with demand_score 5, so it qualifies under the stipulated score threshold. The upstream select_demand function would select records with demand_score >= 3, but normalize filters against an allowed_record_ids list that omits n06-r06 and instead includes n06-r09. As a result, job_1 output contains only seven needs/evidence_sources and job_2 correctly consumes the two handoffs it received, so responsibility localizes to job_1 normalize.
